full_judgment:
3. Mr Khondaker Mahbub Hossain, the learned senior counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the court below without applying its judicial mind and without considering the facts and circumstances, provisions of law most illegally and in an arbitrary manner passed the impugned judgment and order which requires interference by this court. He submits that the plaintiffs admittedly mentioned in the plaint that they become the owner of the suit property by way of registered deed so far it relates to 9.74 acres of land and enjoying the same by constructing house and also they are cultivating the said land. He further submits that the petitioner-plaintiffs filed an application to ascertain the corresponding BS Khatian as well as to ascertain the structures standing thereon and also other places. By referring the deposition of DW 1 he submits that admittedly there are more than 100 acres of land than the land owned by the forest department as much as the DW 1 in his cross-examination categorically stated that he was not aware in whose name the BS Khatian was made. The learned counsel submits that such investigation is very much necessary to ascertain the real question in controversy and to aid the court below come to a conclusion in an appropriate manner. He further submits that they filed the application in a later stage but referring the decisions reported in 25 BLD (AD) 237 as well as 45 DLR 509 submits that a local investigation can be done at any stage of the proceeding and such local investigation is requires for ascertaining the real question in controversy. 

 9. On perusal of the depositions of DW I it transpires that there are more lands in the plot apart from the land owned and claimed by the forest department as much as the DW 1 is not ascertained about the position and other aspects. In the prayer it further transpires that the plaintiffs prayed for local investigation to compare the BS Khatian along with the RS Khatian and also to ascertain certain structures on which they are claiming title and possession in the suit land. There is no denial that such application should be made at the very initial stage but in the decisions reported in 25 BLD (AD) 237 their lordships of our apex court came to a conclusion that it is the duty of the court of law to ascertain all issues before adjudicating the real question in controversy. The intension of our apex court is that the trial court ought to have done any such investigation necessary before passing the decree because no decree can be passed for vague or unidentified land otherwise the decree would be rendered infructuous and a court of law is not supposed to pass a infructuous decree. It has been mentioned earlier that a report of the commissioner pursuant to the provisions of Order 26, rule 9 of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908 is not binding and the court of law is at liberty to accept or refusing in the line of other evidence.
